text: Every admin eventually has to load data from outside ServiceNow — a CSV of new hires from HR, a vendor spreadsheet of assets, a nightly feed from an external database. ServiceNow deliberately never lets that external data write straight into a real table. Instead, it uses a two-stage pattern built directly into the platform: Import Sets.

Stage one is staging. Data from the source lands first in an auto-created Import Set table, prefixed imp underscore, as a raw, completely unmodified copy of whatever arrived. Nothing is validated, cleaned, or mapped yet at this point — it's a landing zone, isolated from anything production-facing, exactly like a staging layer in a data pipeline.

Stage two is the transform. A Transform Map reads those staged rows and maps each staging column to a real field on a target table, like sys_user or a custom CMDB table. Only data that successfully survives this mapping step ever touches a live, production table that real users and processes depend on.

This separation matters because a bad row — a malformed email address, a missing required field — stays visible and fixable sitting inside the staging table. It never corrupts the target table, and an admin can fix the source data or the mapping and simply rerun the transform, without re-downloading or re-uploading anything.

Three pieces work together across this chapter. A Data Source defines where the data actually comes from and is what fills the staging table. The Import Set staging table holds that data raw and untouched. And a Transform Map empties the staging table into something real on the target side.

Staging protects your real data from ever being corrupted by a bad import. Next up: Data Sources — the different real ways external data actually gets into that staging table in the first place, from file uploads to live database connections.
